claims.text: Opsera announced on October 29, 2026 its relaunch as an AI-native software factory with Forge at its center, described as a governed, spec-driven software factory for modernizing legacy estates and building new applications.

Opsera's Forge acts as an enterprise AI harness that turns legacy logic, architecture and business intent into reusable living specs and execution-ready work orders, with a human in the loop and evals, security and compliance checks at every stage.
Opsera claims it can shorten time to market from two weeks to two days, cut token use by up to 75%, save up to $10 million in operating costs, and reduce security reviews from eight weeks to hours.

Opsera's ForgeScore assesses legacy codebases across eight dimensions: security, maintainability, system gravity, production resilience, cognitive load, logic narrative, semantic clarity and future proofing.

Opsera's Forge integrates with Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Antigravity, DeepSeek and Devin, and Opsera connects more than 150 tools; it runs in cloud, on-premises or hybrid environments.

Opsera's Unified Insights uses tokenomics and token mapping to connect AI spend to results across tools, teams and workflows; the portfolio also includes Forge for Salesforce and Forge for Databricks.

Warp's cost per pull request was about $80 at the start, caused by using Opus where not warranted, a triage agent on an unnecessarily high-powered model, and too many sub-agents; after tuning it fell to roughly $15-20 (per Zach Lloyd, Latent Space, recorded early November 2026).
Zach Lloyd of Warp said PR throughput rose 40% over the prior month without an increase in revert rate, which he presented as confidence in the approach rather than a controlled study.

Tereza Tížková of Factory gave an AI Engineer talk, 'Rise of the Software Factory', framing a software factory as the full autonomous lifecycle: signal collection, prioritization, orchestration, execution, validation and iteration.
Gergely Orosz published 'Inside OpenAI's agentic software factory' in The Pragmatic Engineer on September 15, 2026.
Anthropic published 'Agentic coding is straining CI. Here's how we scaled test impact analysis at Anthropic' by Sachin Malhotra on September 14, 2026.
Signadot's October 15, 2026 guide argues most agentic factories close the loop too late because they scaled coding agents rather than the checks that tell them a change works.
Faros AI published 'The Speed Trap: 8 takeaways from Faros's latest AI engineering research' on September 18, 2026.

Augment Code's September 17, 2026 guide defines dark factory software delivery as an unattended delivery line where agents implement and merge changes while humans retain control through gate policy and halt authority.

On the September 3, 2026 SWE-bench Pro snapshot, Muse Spark 1.1 with the mini-swe-agent harness led at 61.50 ± 3.10%; the top SWE-bench Verified entries (Sonar Foundation Agent and live-SWE-agent, both on Claude Opus 4.5) were tied at 79.20%.
Augment Code's Cosmos uses a Verifier Expert that exercises each change against a live environment before a gate accepts it.
CIO Bulletin on October 13, 2026 listed seven enterprise autonomous software factory platforms: Port, GitLab, Harness, Factory, Cognition, GitHub and Tessl.

Port's AI software factory architecture has six pillars: Context Lake, workflows and tools, Port AI, agent management, interface builder and governance; it also introduced Port AI Builder for natural-language agentic workflows.
Harness describes an Autonomous SDLC Platform with a Software Delivery Agent, Autonomous Worker Agents running as pipeline steps, a Knowledge Graph and Harness MCP.
Tessl treats agent skills and context as versioned software assets managed through a registry usable across multiple coding agents.

Oracle introduced Fusion Claw on September 29, 2026, a governed agentic execution runtime supporting 25 new Claw-powered Fusion Agentic Applications, bringing its portfolio to 75, and separating AI judgment from deterministic enterprise computation.
NVIDIA introduced the Open Agent Safety Platform combining the OpenShell secure runtime, the Sentry reference architecture and BlueField-4 DPUs to enforce and contain agent execution.
OpenAI's September 29, 2026 releases introduced dots (always-on agents with their own cloud computers), ChatGPT Space, expanded Codex Cloud, GPT-6.1 Sol and a Decisions API.
OpenClaw introduced OpenClaw Enterprise, an open-source, vendor-neutral, pre-1.0 control plane for persistent agents with multi-tenancy and stronger security boundaries.
Coforge introduced an autonomous software factory for AI-led development, reported by Express Computer on October 29, 2026.
